question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Creature of habit
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I)
options: A faithful dog
A mean person
A bad habit
One who does same thing in the same way
solution:
The correct answer is: One who does same thing in the same way

Explanation:
"Creature of habit" - "आदत का गुलाम"
This idiom refers to a person who follows a fixed routine or repeats the same actions without change, often unconsciously. The correct option fits because it describes someone who consistently behaves in a predictable manner due to ingrained habits.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the observation that humans, like animals, tend to develop repetitive behaviors over time. The word "creature" emphasizes the instinctive, almost automatic nature of habitual actions.

Example:
"John wakes up at 5 AM every day, drinks black coffee, and goes for a run—he's a true creature of habit."
"जॉन हर दिन सुबह 5 बजे उठता है, ब्लैक कॉफी पीता है और दौड़ने जाता है—वह सचमुच आदत का गुलाम है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Creature of habit" is "One who does same thing in the same way" because it describes a person who follows a rigid routine. The other options ("A faithful dog," "A mean person," "A bad habit") do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase to complete the given sentence.

It is easier to learn how a machine works from pictures rather than descriptions, since ________.
(Head Constable Ministerial in Delhi Police Examination 2022)
options: a picture paints a thousand words
it takes a picture
its face is a picture
it is pretty as a picture
solution:
The correct answer is: a picture paints a thousand words 

Explanation:
The sentence emphasizes that visual representations (pictures) are more effective than written or verbal descriptions in explaining how a machine works. The idiom "a picture paints a thousand words" perfectly fits this context, as it means that a single image can convey complex ideas more effectively than a lengthy description.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

a picture paints a thousand words – एक तस्वीर हज़ार शब्दों के बराबर होती है – A visual representation can express complex ideas more powerfully than words.
Example: "Instead of describing the sunset, she showed us a photograph—after all, a picture paints a thousand words."

it takes a picture – यह एक तस्वीर लेता है – This phrase is not a recognized idiom and does not fit the context.
Example: "The device automatically takes a picture when it detects motion." (Literal meaning, not idiomatic)

its face is a picture – इसका चेहरा देखने लायक है – Used when someone’s facial expression is amusing or shocking.
Example: "When he saw the surprise party, his face was a picture!"

it is pretty as a picture – यह तस्वीर की तरह सुंदर है – Used to describe something or someone that looks very beautiful.
Example: "The garden in spring is as pretty as a picture."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "a picture paints a thousand words" is "visuals communicate more effectively than words" because the sentence highlights the superiority of images over text in explaining machinery. The other options either do not fit the context or are unrelated idioms.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
Sarah’s _______________ approach to her responsibilities often lands her in trouble.

(Grade C Stenographers LDC Examination 2020 To 2022)
options: others-may-care
safety-may-care
protection-may-care
devil-may-care
solution:
The correct answer is: devil-may-care

Explanation:
The idiom "devil-may-care" means a reckless or carefree attitude, often without concern for consequences. This fits perfectly in the given sentence, as Sarah’s irresponsible approach leads to trouble.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

others-may-care – [दूसरों की परवाह हो सकती है] – [Not a standard idiom; implies concern from others]
Example: "He acted as if others-may-care, but no one really noticed."

safety-may-care – [सुरक्षा की परवाह हो सकती है] – [Not a standard idiom; implies concern for safety]
Example: "The workers ignored the warnings, thinking safety-may-care."

protection-may-care – [सुरक्षा की परवाह हो सकती है] – [Not a standard idiom; implies concern for protection]
Example: "She left the door unlocked, believing protection-may-care."

devil-may-care – [लापरवाह / बेफिक्र] – [A reckless or carefree attitude]
Example: "His devil-may-care attitude made him ignore all warnings."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "devil-may-care" is "reckless or carefree" because it describes someone who acts without concern for consequences. The other options are either incorrect or not standard idioms.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
It was raining cats and dogs when I reached there.
(MTS Non technical and Havaldar Examination 2021)
options: To rain very heavily
Place full of animals
Lots of appreciation
Not raining at all
solution:
The correct answer is: To rain very heavily

Explanation:
"Raining cats and dogs" - "बहुत तेज बारिश होना"
This idiom is used to describe extremely heavy rainfall. The other options do not relate to the idiom's meaning, as they either misinterpret the phrase or are entirely unrelated.

Origin of the Idiom:
The exact origin is unclear, but one theory suggests that in old European cities, heavy rains would wash dead animals (like cats and dogs) into the streets, making it seem as if they were falling from the sky. Another possibility is that the phrase comes from Norse mythology, where cats and dogs were associated with storms.

Example:
"We had to cancel the picnic because it was raining cats and dogs."
"हमें पिकनिक रद्द करनी पड़ी क्योंकि बहुत तेज बारिश हो रही थी।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "raining cats and dogs" is "to rain very heavily" because it vividly describes intense rainfall. The other options are unrelated to the idiom's true meaning.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.
A fish out of water
(CHSL Exam 2022 Tier I)
options: To criticize someone
To kill somebody
A person out of accustomed environment
A dead person
solution:
The correct answer is: A person out of accustomed environment

Explanation:
"A fish out of water" - "अपने सामान्य वातावरण से बाहर व्यक्ति"
This idiom describes someone who feels uncomfortable or awkward because they are in an unfamiliar situation or environment, just like a fish would struggle if taken out of water.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from the literal image of a fish struggling to survive when removed from its natural habitat (water). Over time, it became a metaphor for humans feeling out of place in unfamiliar surroundings.

Example:
"After moving from a small village to a big city, Ramesh felt like a fish out of water."
"एक छोटे गाँव से बड़े शहर में आने के बाद, रमेश को ऐसा लगा जैसे वह अपनी जगह से बाहर हो।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "A fish out of water" is "A person out of accustomed environment" because it perfectly captures the sense of discomfort in an unfamiliar setting. The other options are unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A slap on the wrist
(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: A tiny gift
A wrist watch
A small punishment
A secret alliance
solution:
The correct answer is: A small punishment

Explanation:
"A slap on the wrist" - "हल्की सजा"
This idiom refers to a minor or lenient punishment given for a wrongdoing, rather than a severe penalty. It implies that the consequence was not very harsh.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the literal act of lightly slapping someone's wrist as a gentle reprimand, often used for children. Over time, it evolved into a metaphorical expression for mild disciplinary actions.

Example:
"The judge gave the offender just a slap on the wrist for his first offense."
"न्यायाधीश ने अपराधी को पहली गलती पर केवल हल्की सजा दी।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "A slap on the wrist" is "A small punishment" because it signifies a mild disciplinary action rather than a severe penalty. The other options ("A tiny gift," "A wrist watch," "A secret alliance") are unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.More to something than meets the eye
(Officer Trainee (Finance))
options: Be simple and straightforward with no hidden details
Have deeper or hidden aspects beyond what is immediately apparent
Have an increased sphere of visibility around the object
Appear insignificant and remain unimportant
solution:
The correct answer is: Have deeper or hidden aspects beyond what is immediately apparent

Explanation:
"More to something than meets the eye" - "सतह से दिखने से अधिक गहराई होना"
This idiom suggests that something is not as simple as it appears and has underlying complexities or hidden aspects that are not immediately noticeable.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the idea that visual perception (what "meets the eye") does not always reveal the full truth. It emphasizes that deeper understanding or investigation is needed to grasp the complete reality.

Example:
"At first glance, the old house seemed abandoned, but there was more to it than meets the eye—it was actually a secret research facility."
"पहली नज़र में, वह पुराना घर खाली लगता था, लेकिन उसके पीछे एक गहरा राज़ था—वह वास्तव में एक गुप्त शोध केंद्र था।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "More to something than meets the eye" is "Have deeper or hidden aspects beyond what is immediately apparent" because it conveys the idea that appearances can be deceiving, and there is often more beneath the surface. The other options do not align with this meaning.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.
To work against the clocks
(MTS Non Tech Havaldar CBIC and CBN Examination 2022)
options: To die while still working
To move anti-clockwise
To fill one with terror
To work fast
solution:
The correct answer is: To work fast

Explanation:
"To work against the clock" - "समय के विरुद्ध काम करना"
This idiom means to work hurriedly to complete something before a deadline. The phrase emphasizes urgency and speed, which aligns with the meaning "to work fast."

Origin of the Idiom:
The expression likely originates from the idea of racing against time, where the "clock" symbolizes a strict deadline. It is commonly used in situations where time is limited, and tasks must be completed quickly.

Example:
"The team was working against the clock to finish the project before the client's deadline."
"टीम क्लाइंट की समय सीमा से पहले प्रोजेक्ट पूरा करने के लिए समय के विरुद्ध काम कर रही थी।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To work against the clock" is "to work fast" because it conveys the urgency of completing a task within a limited time. The other options do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom below.
“Break a leg”

(Constable Tradesman Group C)
options: to be jealous of someone
Slow down
used to wish someone good luck
Used to wish someone bad luck
solution:
The correct answer is: used to wish someone good luck

Explanation:
"Break a leg" - "किसी को शुभकामना देना"
This idiom is commonly used in theatrical and performance contexts to wish someone success before they go on stage. It is a superstitious way of saying "good luck" without actually saying it, as directly wishing good luck was believed to bring bad luck.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originated in the world of theater, where performers believed that saying "good luck" would jinx their performance. Instead, they used the opposite phrase "break a leg" as a way to trick superstition and ensure a successful show.

Example:
"You have an important audition today? Break a leg!"
"आज तुम्हारा एक महत्वपूर्ण ऑडिशन है? ब्रेक अ लेग!"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "break a leg" is "used to wish someone good luck" because it is a traditional way to encourage performers before their act. The other options, such as "to be jealous of someone" or "used to wish someone bad luck," are incorrect interpretations of this idiom.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Beyond the shadow of a doubt
(MTS Non technical and Havaldar Examination 2021)
options: live in fear and uncertainty
With certainty; for sure
located in a remote area
Forget all past problems
solution:
The correct answer is: With certainty; for sure

Explanation:
"Beyond the shadow of a doubt" - "पूर्ण निश्चितता के साथ"
This idiom means that something is absolutely certain and leaves no room for doubt. The phrase emphasizes complete confidence in the truth or accuracy of a statement.

Origin of the Idiom:
The expression likely originates from legal contexts, where proving something "beyond a shadow of a doubt" implies that there is no possible uncertainty remaining. The word "shadow" metaphorically represents even the slightest hint of doubt, so going beyond it means absolute certainty.

Example:
"The evidence proved his innocence beyond the shadow of a doubt."
"सबूतों ने उसकी निर्दोषिता को पूर्ण निश्चितता के साथ साबित कर दिया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Beyond the shadow of a doubt" is "With certainty; for sure" because it conveys absolute confidence without any doubt. The other options do not relate to the idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence.

When he made fun of the sage, who was already infuriated, it made a bad situation worse.
(CHSL Exam 2023 Tier I)
options: Budged up
Made them at the loggerheads
Added fuel to the fire
Pulled someone’s legs
solution:
The correct answer is: Added fuel to the fire

Explanation:
The idiom "added fuel to the fire" means to worsen an already bad situation, which perfectly fits the context where someone's actions aggravated an already angry sage.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

"Budged up" – "हिलना/थोड़ा स्थान देना" – To move slightly or make space for someone.
Example: "Can you budge up a little so I can sit too?"

"Made them at the loggerheads" – "आपस में झगड़ा कराना" – To cause two people or groups to argue or fight.
Example: "His interference made the two friends at loggerheads."

"Added fuel to the fire" – "आग में घी डालना" – To make a bad situation worse.
Example: "By arguing back, she just added fuel to the fire."

"Pulled someone’s legs" – "किसी का मजाक उड़ाना" – To tease or joke with someone.
Example: "He was just pulling your leg; don’t take it seriously."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Added fuel to the fire" is "to worsen an already bad situation" because the sentence describes how mocking the sage further aggravated his anger. The other options do not fit the context.

question:

To believe in selflessness

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To have too many axes to grind" is "To have one’s own interests to serve" because it reflects hidden personal motives. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Beat around the bush
(MTS Non Tech Havaldar CBIC and CBN Examination 2023)
options: To avoid people
To avoid talking about what is important
To talk about important things
To have patience
solution:
The correct answer is: To avoid talking about what is important

Explanation:
"Beat around the bush" - "मुद्दे की बात से बचना"
This idiom means to avoid addressing the main issue directly, often by talking about unimportant or irrelevant details instead.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from hunting practices, where hunters would literally beat bushes to scare birds or animals out into the open. However, those who "beat around the bush" instead of going straight for the target were seen as hesitant or indirect.

Example:
"Stop beating around the bush and tell me what really happened."
"इतना घुमा-फिरा कर बात न करो, सीधे बताओ क्या हुआ।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Beat around the bush" is "To avoid talking about what is important" because it signifies evading the main topic. The other options do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hold your horses
(Constable GD 2021)
options: Make a profit
Take control
Be patient
Run fast
solution:
The correct answer is: Be patient

Explanation:
"Hold your horses" - "धैर्य रखो"
This idiom is used to tell someone to slow down, wait, or be patient, especially when they are acting too quickly or impulsively.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from the literal act of holding back horses to control their speed. It was commonly used in horse-drawn carriage times when riders or drivers needed to steady their horses before moving forward. Over time, it evolved into a figurative expression urging patience.

Example:
"Hold your horses! Let’s think this through before making a decision."
"धैर्य रखो! निर्णय लेने से पहले इस पर विचार कर लें।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Hold your horses" is "Be patient" because it advises someone to wait or slow down. The other options ("Make a profit," "Take control," "Run fast") do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To leave no stone unturned
(SICPO Paper I 2024)
options: To win everything that is available
To control a person completely
To treat someone/something as if of no importance
To do everything possible to achieve something
solution:
The correct answer is: To do everything possible to achieve something

Explanation:
"To leave no stone unturned" - "हर संभव प्रयास करना"
This idiom means making every possible effort to accomplish a goal, ensuring that no opportunity or method is overlooked.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from ancient Greek history. According to legend, the general Polycrates searched for hidden treasure by turning over every stone in a field. Over time, it evolved into a metaphor for thoroughness and exhaustive effort.

Example:
"The detectives left no stone unturned in their search for the missing child."
"गुमशुदा बच्चे की तलाश में जासूसों ने कोई कसर नहीं छोड़ी।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To leave no stone unturned" is "To do everything possible to achieve something" because it signifies exhaustive effort toward a goal. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:

We dodged a bullet when we didn’t fall for the agents’ words.
(SICPO Paper I 2023)
options: To give something a try
To start performing better
To be out of your comfort zone
To narrowly avoid situation
solution:
The correct answer is: To narrowly avoid situation

Explanation:
"dodged a bullet" - "संकट से बच निकलना"
The idiom "dodged a bullet" means to narrowly escape a dangerous or harmful situation. In the given sentence, not falling for the agents’ words helped them avoid a potential problem, which aligns perfectly with this meaning.

Origin of the Idiom:
This phrase originates from the literal act of avoiding a fired bullet in combat, which requires quick reflexes and luck. Over time, it evolved into a metaphor for escaping any kind of trouble or disaster.

Example:
"She missed her flight, but later found out it had crashed—she really dodged a bullet."
"उसकी फ्लाइट छूट गई, लेकिन बाद में पता चला कि वह क्रैश हो गई थी—वह वाकई संकट से बच गई।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "dodged a bullet" is "to narrowly avoid a dangerous or harmful situation" because it describes escaping an unfavorable outcome by a close margin. The other options do not relate to the idiom’s intended meaning.

question:

You should stop interfering unnecessarily in the affairs of others.
(Head Constable Ministerial)
options: poking your nose
making amends
paying through your nose
playing fast and loose
solution:
The correct answer is: poking your nose

Explanation:
The idiom "poking your nose" means interfering in someone else's business unnecessarily, which fits perfectly with the given sentence.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

poking your nose – [दूसरों के मामलों में दखल देना] – [To interfere in someone else's business without being asked]
Example: "Stop poking your nose into my personal matters!"

making amends – [गलती सुधारना] – [To compensate for a mistake or wrongdoing]
Example: "He apologized and tried to make amends for his rude behavior."

paying through your nose – [बहुत ज्यादा कीमत चुकाना] – [To pay an excessively high price for something]
Example: "We had to pay through our nose for those concert tickets."

playing fast and loose – [बेईमानी से व्यवहार करना] – [To behave irresponsibly or deceitfully]
Example: "He played fast and loose with the company's finances and got fired."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "poking your nose" is "interfering unnecessarily in others' affairs" because it directly matches the context of the given sentence. The other options are unrelated to the idea of unwanted interference.

The idiom comes from the literal act of marking checkboxes on forms or lists to indicate that all conditions have been satisfied. Over time, it evolved into a figurative expression for meeting expectations.

Example:
"The new candidate ticks all the boxes for the job—experience, skills, and attitude."
"नया उम्मीदवार नौकरी के लिए सभी शर्तों को पूरा करता है—अनुभव, कौशल और रवैया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Tick all the boxes" is "To fulfill the required norms" because it signifies meeting all necessary conditions. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
I tried to tell him to think of the good times, that every cloud has a silver lining.
(MTS Non technical and Havaldar Examination 2021)
options: Doing something with thoroughness and passion
Don’t cry over what has happened as it cannot be fixed
Treat people the same way as you want to be treated
Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it
solution:
The correct answer is: Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it

Explanation:
"Every cloud has a silver lining" - "हर मुश्किल स्थिति में एक उम्मीद की किरण होती है"
This idiom means that no matter how bad a situation may seem, there is always some positive aspect or hope to be found in it.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from the idea that even the darkest clouds have a bright, silvery edge when the sun shines behind them. It was popularized by John Milton in his 1634 poem Comus, where he wrote, "Was I deceived, or did a sable cloud / Turn forth her silver lining on the night?"

Example:
"After losing his job, he started his own business—proving that every cloud has a silver lining."
"नौकरी खोने के बाद, उसने अपना खुद का व्यवसाय शुरू किया—यह साबित करता है कि हर बादल के पीछे सूरज छिपा होता है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it" is "there is always something positive in a bad situation" because the idiom emphasizes optimism in adversity. The other options are unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the correct meaning of the idiom “the grass is greener on the other side” from the given options:
(Group D posts)
options: perception that other people are not desirable and should not be chased
perception that other people or places are more desirable than one's current situation
perception that one's current situation is most desirable
to be satisfied in own life
solution:
The correct answer is: perception that other people or places are more desirable than one's current situation

Explanation:
"the grass is greener on the other side" - "दूसरी जगह की घास हमेशा हरी लगती है"
This idiom expresses the common human tendency to believe that others' circumstances are better than one's own, even when that may not be true.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the observation that grass appears greener from a distance but may not be so upon closer inspection. It has been used in English literature since at least the 19th century to highlight the folly of dissatisfaction with one's own situation.

Example:
"She always thinks her friends have better lives, but the grass is greener on the other side."
"वह हमेशा सोचती है कि उसके दोस्तों की ज़िंदगी बेहतर है, लेकिन दूसरी जगह की घास हमेशा हरी लगती है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "the grass is greener on the other side" is "perception that other people or places are more desirable than one's current situation" because it captures the essence of envying others' seemingly better circumstances. The other options either contradict or do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.To bite off more than you can chew
(Junior Accounts Officer)
options: To eat too much food
To try to do something that is too difficult
To be overly lazy in doing work
To take on a task that is easy
solution:
The correct answer is: To try to do something that is too difficult

Explanation:
"To bite off more than you can chew" - "जितनी चबाने की क्षमता हो, उससे ज्यादा निवाला लेना"
This idiom means attempting to do something that is beyond one's capability or capacity, leading to difficulty in completing it.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from the literal act of taking a larger bite of food than one can comfortably chew. Over time, it evolved into a metaphor for taking on more responsibilities or challenges than one can handle.

Example:
"He agreed to organize three events in one week but soon realized he had bitten off more than he could chew."
"उसने एक हफ्ते में तीन कार्यक्रम आयोजित करने की जिम्मेदारी ली, लेकिन जल्द ही उसे एहसास हुआ कि उसने अपनी क्षमता से ज्यादा काम ले लिया है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To bite off more than you can chew" is "To try to do something that is too difficult" because it perfectly captures the idea of overestimating one's ability to handle a task. The other options do not align with the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hit the sack
(Constable GD 2021)
options: Go to bed
Find a treasure
Work hard
Fool someone
solution:
The correct answer is: Go to bed

Explanation:
"Hit the sack" - "सोने जाना"
The idiom "hit the sack" means to go to bed or to go to sleep. It is a casual and informal way of saying someone is going to rest.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the early 20th century when mattresses were often filled with sacks of straw or other materials. "Hitting the sack" referred to lying down on such a mattress to sleep.

Example:
"I'm exhausted after work; I'm going to hit the sack early tonight."
"काम के बाद मैं बहुत थक गया हूँ; आज रात मैं जल्दी सोने जा रहा हूँ।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Hit the sack" is "Go to bed" because it directly refers to the act of going to sleep. The other options ("Find a treasure," "Work hard," "Fool someone") are unrelated to this idiom.
